dedupe_keys.name: eurdep european radiological data exchange platform near real time gamma dose rates about 5 000 stations

description: EURDEP, the European Radiological Data Exchange Platform, is the data exchange mechanism and website run by the European Commission Joint Research Centre for radiological monitoring data shared by 39 participating countries in almost real time. It is the EU official tool for exchanging radiological data in an emergency, under Council Decision 87/600 (ECURIE) and Recommendation 2000/473/Euratom, but data flow continuously so that in normal times it reflects natural background radiation. National networks send routine data at least daily, and hourly in an emergency; the platform mirrors data across servers and forwards an hourly aggregate to the IAEA IRMIS system. The public Advanced map shows hourly gamma dose rate averages going back up to 35 days from about 5,000 stations; the Simple map was discontinued on 31 July 2023. EURDEP also defines a data format, used since 2002 and IRIX compliant since 2013. Coverage is Europe. Public viewing is free; unlimited access to all data through web services is for authorised users, and some countries delay public release by up to 999 hours. Caveats: it is not an alert system, and no open bulk download or data licence is stated. Simulation uses are exposure mapping and emergency response scenarios after nuclear plant accidents. Related records: data-bfs-odl-ambient-gamma-dose-rate-network-germany is one national network that feeds such platforms.
